text: On the next market day. <break time="0.8s" /> He went to Goderville. <break time="0.8s" /> Only to tell his story. <break time="0.8s" /> But Malandain laughed. <break time="0.8s" /> When he passed. <break time="0.8s" /> A farmer did not even let him finish. <break time="0.8s" /> But tapped him on the stomach. <break time="0.8s" /> And cried. <break time="0.8s" /> Get along, you old rascal. <break time="0.8s" /> At the inn. <break time="0.8s" /> A horse dealer laughed and said that he knew all about that old trick. <break time="0.8s" /> With the string. <break time="0.8s" /> But they found the pocketbook. <break time="0.8s" /> Stammered Hauchecorne. <break time="0.8s" /> And the dealer replied. <break time="0.8s" /> One man finds it. <break time="0.8s" /> And another man returns it. <break time="0.8s" /> Suddenly he understood that people thought. <break time="0.8s" /> A partner had returned the money for him. <break time="0.8s" /> He went home in shame and anger. <break time="0.8s" /> For he knew that he was sly enough. <break time="0.8s" /> To play such a trick. <break time="0.8s" /> If he had the chance. <break time="0.8s" /> He would even boast of such a trick. <break time="0.8s" /> And the whole town knew it. <break time="0.8s" /> He made his story longer each day. <break time="0.8s" /> But the more he explained. <break time="0.8s" /> The less people believed him. <break time="0.8s" /> He grew thinner and weaker. <break time="0.8s" /> And jokers made him tell. <break time="0.8s" /> The story of the string. <break time="0.8s" /> Just to laugh at him. <break time="0.8s" /> He fell ill in December. <break time="0.8s" /> And died in January. <break time="0.8s" /> Repeating A little piece of string. <break time="0.8s" /> Look, here it is, Mister Mayor.
